context: Support session for Basil Kitchen, a restaurant group with an ordering app. Contact: Leo Hart, operations. The app takes card payments through a provider called Paygate. Kitchen printers are connected through a small box in each branch. The support plan covers 6 hours a month. The last release went out on Monday.

lines.text: Hello Leo, Sam here from support. Your ticket is open on my screen.

lines.speaker: Leo
lines.text: Thanks Sam. Kim is with me, she runs our busiest branch.
Good. Describe the symptoms in your own words.

lines.speaker: Leo
lines.text: On Android phones the app closes by itself at the exact moment the customer presses pay.
I will pull the crash reports for the last release.

lines.speaker: Kim
lines.text: In the kitchen every order prints twice, so the cooks make double meals and we waste food.
Duplicate prints often come from a retry, I will look there.

lines.speaker: Kim
lines.text: Yesterday alone we threw away about forty meals because of the double prints.
That is a real cost, I will put it in the ticket.

lines.speaker: Leo
lines.text: The estimated delivery time in the app always shows thirty minutes, even on a rainy Friday night.
A fixed estimate sounds like a default value, I will check.

lines.speaker: Leo
lines.text: Our owner is furious since the release went out on Monday and she wants it rolled back today.
I understand the pressure, let me see the effect of a rollback.

lines.speaker: Kim
lines.text: Two branches have already stopped taking app orders and send people to the phone line.

lines.speaker: Leo
lines.text: Kim just told me the new coffee machine arrived and it is huge.
That sounds exciting for the branch.

lines.speaker: Kim
lines.text: It makes a lot of noise, I hope you cannot hear it.
